title: Phase 01 — Foundations (0–3 years)
primaryObjective: Attachment, safety, and sensory exploration — a secure base from which the child explores the world.
summary: The first three years build the foundation for everything that follows. Through responsive, loving care the child develops secure attachment, a sense of safety, and the drive to explore. Learning here is not academic: it is sensory, physical, relational, and playful. The caregiver is the primary 'application' — the platform's role is to guide and support the caregiver in creating rich, safe opportunities for the child to develop.
guidingPrinciple: Responsive, warm interaction — serve and return — is the engine of early development. The platform supports the caregiver; it never replaces the relationship.

developmentDomains.focus: Gross and fine motor development: head control, rolling, sitting, crawling, walking, climbing, grasping, scribbling, stacking.
Creating a safe environment and building the child's earliest sense of a secure base and trusted adults.
Feeding, sleep, nutrition, handwashing habits, and the first steps of self-feeding and dressing.
Sensory play, cause-and-effect toys, imitation, and open-ended exploration of objects and spaces.
Babbling, first words, naming, back-and-forth 'conversation', songs, and shared book-looking.
Co-regulation of emotions through comfort, naming feelings, and predictable routines.
Secure attachment, turn-taking, early sharing, and warmth toward familiar people.

yearPlans.label: Year 1 (0–12 months)
objectives: Establish secure attachment through consistent, responsive care.
Support sensory and motor development from reflexes to sitting and first crawling.
Begin serve-and-return interactions: respond to the baby's sounds, gestures, and gazes.
Establish safe sleep, feeding, and daily rhythm.
capabilities: Holds head steady; rolls over; sits with and then without support.
Tracks faces and objects; reaches for and grasps objects.
Babbles and responds to familiar voices; turns to name.
Shows comfort-seeking and stranger awareness (healthy attachment signs).

yearPlans.label: Year 2 (12–24 months)
objectives: Encourage walking, climbing, and active exploration in safe spaces.
Grow vocabulary through naming, narration, and shared reading.
Introduce simple choices and routines that build early independence.
Support emotional co-regulation as the toddler meets frustration.
capabilities: Walks independently; begins to run and climb.
Uses several single words and begins two-word combinations.
Points to show interest; imitates adults and other children.
Begins self-feeding with fingers and a spoon; helps with dressing.

yearPlans.label: Year 3 (24–36 months)
objectives: Expand language into short sentences and simple questions.
Encourage pretend play, building, and simple problem-solving.
Support early emotional vocabulary: naming feelings together.
Build everyday self-care routines (handwashing, tidying up, dressing).
capabilities: Speaks in short sentences; follows two-step instructions.
Engages in pretend play and simple cooperative play.
Sorts shapes and colours; completes simple puzzles.
Shows growing independence and expresses a wide range of emotions.

daily.title: Serve and return
daily.description: Notice the baby's sounds, faces, and gestures and respond warmly in turn — the back-and-forth that builds the brain.

daily.title: Tummy time & floor play
daily.description: Supervised time on the tummy and floor to build strength and encourage reaching, rolling, and crawling.

daily.title: Narrate the day
daily.description: Talk through everyday routines ('Now we wash your hands') to flood the child with language.

daily.title: Shared book-looking
daily.description: Look at a picture book together daily, naming and pointing — no need to read every word.

weekly.title: Sensory exploration tray
weekly.description: Offer safe, varied textures and materials to touch and explore under supervision.

weekly.title: Outdoor exploration
weekly.description: Time outside to watch, hear, and touch the natural world — leaves, grass, light, sound.

weekly.title: Music and movement
weekly.description: Sing, clap, and move together to build rhythm, listening, and joyful connection.

parentGuidance.guidance: In these years your warm, responsive presence does more for the child's brain than any product. The platform's job is to support you, not to come between you and your child.

When your baby coos, points, or reaches, respond — look, name, smile, hand it over. This simple back-and-forth is the single most powerful early-learning activity, backed by the Harvard Center on the Developing Child.
Offer safe opportunities and let curiosity drive. You do not need flashcards; you need conversation, play, and safety.

For children under about two, real interaction beats screens. Prioritise faces, voices, and hands-on play. When in doubt about your child's development, talk to your paediatrician — the platform never replaces that.

milestones.description: Shows comfort-seeking and attachment to caregivers

safety.guidance: Follow current safe-sleep guidance (back to sleep, firm flat surface, no loose bedding) to reduce the risk of sleep-related infant death. Confirm specifics with your paediatrician.
As the child becomes mobile, secure furniture, cover outlets, lock away chemicals and medicines, and keep small objects out of reach to prevent choking.
Never leave a child unattended near water, cooking, or hot liquids. Set water heaters to a safe temperature.
Emotional safety matters as much as physical safety. Consistent, comforting responses tell the child the world is safe to explore.

outcomes: The child shows signs of secure attachment and seeks comfort from trusted caregivers.
The child reaches gross and fine motor milestones within typical, flexible ranges.
The child communicates with words, gestures, and short sentences by age three.
The child engages in curious, exploratory, and pretend play.
The caregiver can describe and create safe, language-rich, play-based daily routines.

projects.title: Our family routine chart
projects.description: Caregiver builds a simple visual daily rhythm (sleep, meals, play, outdoor time) with the platform's guidance, adapting it to the child.

projects.title: A homemade sensory basket
projects.description: Assemble a basket of safe household objects of different textures, weights, and sounds for the child to explore under supervision.

projects.title: First words journal
projects.description: Caregiver notes new sounds and words to celebrate progress and spot when to seek a professional's input — never as a competitive scorecard.

appFeatures.userJourney: A parent opens the app and sees today's age-appropriate serve-and-return prompt, one play idea, and one safety reminder — short enough to do in minutes.
A caregiver gently logs milestones and receives supportive, non-alarming context, with a clear prompt to consult a paediatrician for concerns.
A caregiver browses hands-on activities filtered by development domain and the materials they have at home.
A caregiver works through an age-staged home-safety checklist that updates as the child becomes mobile.
